summary:
LUNAR MISSION – Lunar Science Explorer

LUNAR MISSION is an interactive lunar exploration platform designed to support the identification and evaluation of potential Moon landing sites. The project combines a 3D lunar visualization with scientific data analysis tools, including elevation and slope measurements based on NASA’s Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) dataset.

Users can explore the lunar surface, examine different regions, visualize craters and surface features, and compare potential landing locations through an interactive mission control interface. The platform aims to make complex lunar data more accessible and understandable while supporting safer and more informed landing site assessments.

This project addresses the challenge of identifying suitable lunar landing areas by bringing important surface information together in one accessible platform. Understanding elevation, terrain slope, craters, and permanently shadowed regions is essential for future lunar missions, astronaut safety, and scientific exploration.

Our goal is to make lunar exploration more interactive, accessible, and data-driven, contributing to humanity’s future efforts to explore and understand the Moon.
details:
LUNAR MISSION CONTROL: Lunar Science Explorer

LUNAR MISSION CONTROL is an interactive lunar exploration platform developed to help users explore the Moon and evaluate potential landing regions. It combines a 3D lunar visualization with terrain analysis features, allowing users to examine lunar regions, explore surface characteristics, and review elevation and slope measurements.

The project uses NASA's Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation dataset to provide information about the Moon's surface. Users can interact with the mission control interface, explore different regions, view terrain layers, and compare sample landing locations. The platform is designed to make lunar scientific information easier to understand through visual and interactive tools.

One of its main benefits is bringing different types of lunar surface information together in one accessible interface. This can support early mission planning, educational activities, and discussions about suitable landing regions. Our intended impact is to contribute to more accessible lunar exploration and encourage interest in space science and future Moon missions.

We developed the project using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the frontend, and Python with FastAPI for the backend. NumPy was used to process NASA LOLA elevation data. We also used NASA's publicly available lunar datasets as our scientific data foundation.

What makes LUNAR MISSION CONTROL creative is its combination of interactive visualization and scientific data in a single mission-control experience. Instead of presenting lunar information only as numbers or static images, it allows users to explore and interpret terrain information visually.

During development, our team considered data accessibility, user experience, terrain characteristics, elevation, slope, crater distribution, and the importance of permanently shadowed regions. We also considered the need to distinguish between demonstration results and scientifically validated landing-site assessments.
